name: Erewash

licensing.additional: Mandatory HMO licensing applies (five or more people from two or more households); the council keeps a public register of licensed HMOs and said in February 2026 it was stepping up action to make sure all HMOs are licensed. No additional HMO licensing scheme was found.

councilTax.text: £2,360.64 average Band D (2026/27), including Derbyshire County Council, police, fire and average parish precepts

neighbourhoods.name: Ilkeston
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian and Edwardian terraces around the town centre, with interwar and post-war council-built estates and newer estates on the edges.

neighbourhoods.name: Long Eaton
neighbourhoods.housing: Rows of Victorian and Edwardian terraces from the lace and furniture-making era, with interwar semis and some converted mills.

neighbourhoods.name: Sandiacre
neighbourhoods.housing: Terraced and semi-detached houses alongside the Erewash Canal, with some newer infill estates.

neighbourhoods.name: Kirk Hallam
neighbourhoods.housing: A large post-war estate of former council houses and flats south-west of Ilkeston.

neighbourhoods.name: Sawley
neighbourhoods.housing: Older village houses near the Trent with suburban semis and bungalows.

neighbourhoods.name: Borrowash and Ockbrook
neighbourhoods.housing: Villages of semi-detached and detached houses and bungalows between Derby and Long Eaton.

neighbourhoods.name: Draycott and Breaston
neighbourhoods.housing: Villages with brick cottages and terraces in their centres and post-war suburban housing around them.

neighbourhoods.name: West Hallam
neighbourhoods.housing: A largely owner-occupied village of post-war semis and detached houses.

neighbourhoods.name: Spondon fringe and Breadsall
neighbourhoods.housing: Small villages of older cottages and larger detached houses on the edge of Derby.

housing: Erewash is centred on two former industrial towns, Ilkeston and Long Eaton, where Victorian and Edwardian terraces make up much of the rented stock. Large post-war estates such as Kirk Hallam sit alongside newer private estates, while the villages between Derby and Nottingham are mostly owner-occupied semis and bungalows. Private renting is close to the Derbyshire average overall but higher in central Ilkeston, and the council has been working to bring unlicensed HMOs into licensing.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Ilkeston and Long Eaton: photograph rear yards, outhouses, shared alleys (gennels) and any damp at the base of walls.
Older terraced houses often have solid walls and small rear kitchens: check for condensation and mould in kitchens, bathrooms and back bedrooms.
Homes near the Trent and the Erewash Canal in Sawley and Sandiacre: note any signs of past flooding or damp in ground-floor rooms.
Post-war ex-council houses in Kirk Hallam: record the boiler, windows and doors, and the condition of gardens and fencing.
Shared houses in Ilkeston town centre: photograph each room's lock, furniture and fire door, and note smoke alarms and the fire blanket.
Village bungalows in Borrowash and Breaston: check garages, drives and garden sheds, which are often included in the let.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Erewash Borough Council's private sector housing team (environmental health), after first telling their landlord.
